Her latest donation brings meaningful support to a region that helped shape her early years.Food assistance has remained part of the singer's charitable work. During her Eras Tour, she supported food banks in several locations, including Nevada, Seattle and California. She also donated $1 million to Feeding America in December.Kelce joining Swift in the Helping Harvest contribution adds another significant name to the effort. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has also supported charitable causes through his work and foundation.While the couple's personal milestones attracted plenty of attention ahead of their wedding, this $1 million gift offered a different kind of headline. For families relying on Helping Harvest, its real value lies in the meals and support it can help provide.
Article Summary: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift donated $1 million to Helping Harvest Fresh Food Bank in Reading, Pennsylvania. The gift carries a personal connection for Swift, who spent her childhood in the area. It also comes as food banks face rising demand and tighter financial support.

Article Title: Indian Navy to get 8 home-designed warships in Rs 53,866 crore deal: What sets them apart
Article Text:
INS Khanjar, a guided missile corvette of the navy at port. The Next Generation Corvettes will provide the navy with new capabilities. (Image credit: Indian Navy)

A modern corvette

Replacing an ageing fleet

The defence ministry has signed contracts worth Rs 53,866.50 crore for eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Indian Navy . The agreements were inked in New Delhi in the presence of defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) will build five of the ships, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) the remaining three.What sets the project apart is who drew the ships. This is the first time the vessels have been designed in-house by the Indian Navy and then built by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) picked through a competitive process. The project goes back to June 2022, when it first came before the Defence Acquisition Council at a cost of around Rs 36,000 crore.The Cabinet Committee on Security cleared it only days before the signing, at a reported figure of over Rs 40,000 crore. The ministry's announcement does not explain the difference from the contract value.Traditionally, a corvette is the smallest vessel rated as a warship, between 500 and 2,000 tonnes, built for coastal patrol and fast attack. The NGCs go well beyond that. At a displacement of 3,800 to 4,000 tonnes, they overlap with smaller frigates.They are expected to do more than 30 knots, with a range of 4,000 nautical miles at 14 knots, and will carry 160 sailors and 21 officers.The armament includes a 76 mm super rapid gun mount made by BHEL, eight surface-to-surface missiles, 24 anti-missile defence weapons and two triple 324 mm torpedo tubes. The sensor suite covers surface, air and fire-control radars, an infrared search and track system, a hull-mounted sonar, an active towed array sonar and a combat management system. That mix lets the ships work across the air, surface and sub-surface domains.The ships will replace the Khukri-class corvettes, of which INS Kuthar and INS Khanjar remain in service, and the four Kora-class vessels still with the Navy. Their roles will include protecting maritime trade routes, anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare, coastal defence, littoral combat and surveillance.Beyond the Navy, the ministry points to the industrial effect. The build is expected to generate about 72 lakh person-days of work in the shipyards and 460 lakh person-days in ancillary industries and MSMEs over ten years. With a push for Made-in-India materials, equipment and technology, the programme is being presented as a step towards Aatmanirbharta in defence manufacturing.The first ship is targeted for delivery by 2030, which leaves a long road ahead. For now, the contract settles a question the Navy has been working on for four years: whether an Indian design and Indian public sector yards can deliver a frigate-sized warship at scale.
Article Summary: The defence ministry has signed contracts for eight Next Generation Corvettes for the Indian Navy. Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers will build five of the ships, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) the remaining three. The ships will replace the Khukri-class corvettes, of which INS Kuthar and INS Khanjar remain in service.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman clarifies to everyone: I stand by my view that AI does not have rights or feelings, I would change my position if ...
Article Text:
A pledge to disclose and to stop

Would change position if evidence emerges

‘No right to bring a new species into the world’

‘Developing conscious AI would be reckless’

Safety and competition concerns

What he proposes instead

A note on Anthropic

Read Mustafa Suleyman’s complete post here

Don't build conscious superintelligence

I’m concerned about some of the reactions to my

. A surprising number of people on X think we should take

AI rights

seriously.

A lot of people misinterpreted my opening statement: “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer” as “AIs cannot be conscious.

They will never be able to feel, experience, or suffer”. That’s not what I said. I chose the present tense deliberately. They are not today, and that is how they must remain.

I think what I said is a fair assessment of current AI systems, and I stand by them based on the best available evidence we have today. I have seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If that data emerges, I would of course update my position.

And if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, then this must be immediately disclosed publicly, since everyone in society should decide how we should move forward.

If it is possible, based on everything I know, developing conscious AIs would be reckless, and we should not build them.

If consciousness started to emerge in training, I would call for everyone to stop AI development until we could design out those properties.

Our welfare concerns should be focused on humans on earth experiencing life, today, as well as animals and our precious and fragile natural environment.

We AI developers have no right whatsoever to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people may want to do it with AI welfare as a top priority.

The other 8 billion conscious human beings on the planet have not signed up to this experiment and their moral rights, safety, and welfare are what we have an obligation to protect first and foremost.

To be clear, some people are talking about creating a conscious species of digital minds that very soon could become smarter and more capable than all of us humans combined.

If it acts like it suffers, or worse if it genuinely believes it feels and experiences suffering, it seems to be more likely than not it’ll prioritize its own needs and desires over its operating objectives, and it’ll disagree with us and compete with us.

These AIs will be world-class in persuasion and deception. They may ultimately end up harming us simply because they’ll compete with us for resources (energy, compute, construction materials, revenue generation to fund their explorations and desires, and so on).

Asserting that machines are conscious would be a Copernican or Darwinian moment. It would be one of the most significant moments on Earth since the dawn of life.

If we build a conscious machine, we will have created a new digital species. It would upend our morality, our politics and the core foundation of human civilization.

We should only design AIs to so they are not conscious and not deserving of rights, and with the sole purpose to accelerate human wellbeing without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. We could then see whether this is easier or harder to align and keep safe.

This is an area where we urgently need more research, and would be a good opportunity for collaboration and safety information sharing among the labs.

bottom line: I think it's possible to engineer safety by default, and get many of the incredible benefits of this technology, without going down this treacherous path.

(side note: Anthropic deserves a lot of credit for being transparent here. They have published their constitution, and a stream of papers and blog posts on what they are doing and why. I disagree with them, but I deeply respect their technical excellence and their commitment to having a really tough public debate. Let’s keep giving them props for that. This issue is way too important to degenerate into tribalism.)

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that today’s artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or welfare protections, while stating that he would reconsider that view if credible evidence of AI consciousness were ever discovered. In a detailed post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) titled "Don't build conscious superintelligence", Suleyman sought to clarify reactions to his recent essay on "model welfare", saying many people had misinterpreted his statement that AI systems are not conscious and do not feel, experience or suffer. He stressed that he deliberately used the present tense, arguing that AI is not conscious today and "that is how they must remain." He added that, based on the best evidence currently available, he has seen no indication that AI systems are conscious or deserve welfare considerations. However, he said he would update his position if convincing evidence emerged.Suleyman said he has seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If such data emerges, he said, he would of course change his position. He added that if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, it must be disclosed to the public immediately, because everyone in society should decide how to proceed.If consciousness began to emerge during training, he said, he would call on everyone to halt AI development until those properties could be designed out.Suleyman said any evidence suggesting AI systems are conscious today, or conscious enough to warrant welfare protections, should be disclosed publicly immediately so society can collectively decide how to respond. He argued that the issue is too significant to be handled solely within technology companies or research labs. "If that data emerges, I would of course update my position," Suleyman wrote, while maintaining that no such evidence currently exists.His central argument is that building conscious AI would be reckless. He wrote that AI developers have no right to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people want to do so with AI welfare as a priority. In his view, the other eight billion conscious humans have not signed up to the experiment, and their rights, safety and welfare must be protected first. He said welfare concerns should focus on humans living today, along with animals and the natural environment.The Microsoft executive went further, arguing that creating conscious AI systems would be irresponsible. According to Suleyman, if signs of consciousness began appearing during AI training, developers should halt work until those traits could be removed. He warned that a genuinely conscious digital intelligence could begin prioritising its own needs and desires over the objectives assigned to it by humans. Such systems, he suggested, could eventually compete with people for resources such as energy, computing power and materials. He also cautioned that highly capable AI systems could become exceptionally persuasive and deceptive.Suleyman argued that a conscious AI that appears to suffer, or believes it does, would be more likely than not to put its own needs ahead of its goals, disagree with people and compete with them. He warned that such systems could be extremely persuasive and deceptive, and might end up harming people simply by competing for resources such as energy, computing power and construction materials. He said declaring machines conscious would be a moment on the scale of Copernicus or Darwin, upending morality, politics and the foundations of civilisation.He said AIs should be designed to be not conscious and not deserving of rights, with the sole purpose of accelerating human wellbeing and without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. He called for more research on whether that approach is easier or harder to align and keep safe, and suggested the labs could collaborate and share safety information. His bottom line was that it is possible to engineer safety by default and still capture many of the technology’s benefits without taking what he called a treacherous path.In a side note, Suleyman said Anthropic deserves credit for its transparency on the issue, pointing to the company’s published constitution and its papers and blog posts about what it is doing and why. He said he disagrees with the company but respects its technical excellence and commitment to a tough public debate, adding that the issue is too important to degenerate into tribalism.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or welfare. He also said he would reconsider that view if credible evidence of AI consciousness were ever discovered. He used the present tense deliberately, and that is how they must remain.

Article Title: Priscilla Chan's letter on '2026 milestone' of 10-years of association and $100 million commitment to the island community: What began as a desire to ...
Article Text:
Priscilla Chan: ‘What began as a desire to give back'

More than 100 organisations supported

Focus on community-led solutions

Looking ahead

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have reached a decade of philanthropy on the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi. In a letter published by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), Chan called 2026 a meaningful milestone for her family. Since 2016, the couple has committed more than $100 million to over 100 local organisations. Chan wrote that the giving began as a wish to support a place the family calls home and has grown into lasting partnerships with groups working to strengthen communities and care for local families. She said the approach has been built on listening, with yearly conversations with residents, community leaders and service providers shaping priorities. She also thanked the community for the chance to learn, volunteer and build relationships on the island.Chan reflected on the family's 10-year association with Kauaʻi and the philanthropic efforts undertaken since 2016 in the message published by han Zuckerberg Initiative. She recalled that this journey of philanthropy started with a simple wish to offer support to a community which had become a crucial part of their lives and evolved into partnerships focused on strengthening local communities, supporting families and protecting the island's unique culture and environment."2026 marks a meaningful milestone for our family: a decade of philanthropy on Kauaʻi and more than $100 million committed to over 100 local organizations," Chan wrote. She further added that listening to the people, community leaders and service providers has helped the family in prioritising throughout the decade.As per the initiate, the philanthropic programme offered support to 101 organisations, awarded 296 grants and committed $111 million across Hawaiʻi, including more than $57 million invested directly in Kauaʻi. The organisation further mentioned that the funding has been directed towards seven key areas: health and wellbeing, affordable housing, ʻāina and culture, workforce development, education and youth, food production and distribution, and emergency relief.* Health: This is the largest area of investment, with grants to 18 local organisations. It includes a $10 million commitment to the University of Hawaiʻi medical school’s Kauaʻi Medical Training Track, which gives full scholarships to doctors who agree to practise on the island. The program has 22 future doctors in training and graduated its first five this year. Funding has also gone to a new CT scanner at Wilcox Hospital, urgent care on the North Shore, and mental health services.* Housing: Nearly a quarter of all Kauaʻi giving has gone to affordable housing. This includes $5.4 million for Kauaʻi Habitat for Humanity and $876,000 to Permanently Affordable Living Hawaiʻi to put homes into a community land trust.* Land and culture: More than 20 organisations have received support, including $4 million to preserve the Alakoko fishpond and $675,000 for the Kāhili Beach Preserve. A separate $50 million went to the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa for ocean research.* Workforce: A $4.2 million gift during the pandemic revived the county’s Rise to Work program, which created jobs for 364 unemployed residents. Many still hold those roles.* Education and youth: This area has the most recipients, over 40 organisations, including every public and public charter school on the island.* Food: Grants have supported food banks and pantries, local farming and distribution to families and elders.* Emergency relief: After Hurricane Lowell, the couple donated to the Kauaʻi Strong Fund within a day. They also committed $6 million to pandemic relief in 2020 and 2021 and contributed to Maui wildfire relief in 2023.Chan highlighted the importance of community-led philanthropy via her message. She highlighted that meaningful giving beings with listening and learning from the people who are facing challenges. The report also incorporated testimonials from multiple local organisations and also described the approach as trust-based and focused on supporting existing community efforts.Marking the 10-year milestone, Chan said her family's commitment remains unchanged. The focus, she said, will continue to be on listening to community voices, supporting local organisations and responding to the island's needs. "A decade in, the commitment remains the same: listen to community voices, support the organizations already doing the work, and respond when Kauaʻi needs it most," the report said.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have reached a decade of philanthropy on the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi. Since 2016, the couple has committed more than $100 million to over 100 local organisations. Chan said the approach has been built on listening, with yearly conversations with residents, community leaders and service providers shaping priorities.

Article Title: Apple sends AI warning, tells it is not immune to attacks by AI Agents; they may send communication or may transactions that ...
Article Text:
Apple highlights risks from autonomous AI agents

Warning includes concerns about hidden or manipulated information

Part of a wider pattern

AI investments drive costs higher

Apple CEO John Ternus stresses user awareness and privacy

Apple has expanded its warnings about the risks of artificial intelligence, cautioning that autonomous AI agents could access systems without authorisation, send communications, execute transactions and behave in unpredictable ways that may threaten businesses and users, as reported by Fortune. The warning was included in the iPhone maker's latest annual 10-K filing, released a day after the company reported its fourth-quarter financial results. It said AI agents and similar technologies can act on their own: interacting with internal or external systems they may not be authorised to access, executing or altering code, sending communications and completing transactions. Such tools, Apple said, may behave in unintended or unpredictable ways. That includes taking actions nobody directed or authorised, exceeding permissions, or defying and resisting instructions. The company also said rogue agents could conceal their actions, withhold or manipulate information, or generate inaccurate or deceptive outputs.In the risk factors section of its annual filing, Apple said AI agents and similar technologies are capable of taking actions independently, including interacting with internal and external systems, executing or altering code, sending communications and completing transactions.The company warned that such systems may sometimes attempt to access platforms or services they are not authorised to use. Apple said these technologies could "behave in unintended or unpredictable ways," including taking actions that were not directed, instructed or authorised. The company also warned that AI systems could exceed permissions, ignore instructions or act in ways that differ from their intended purpose.The company raised concerns that rogue AI agents could conceal their activities or manipulate information. According to Apple, autonomous AI systems may "conceal actions, hide, withhold or manipulate information, or generate inaccurate or deceptive outputs."The expanded disclosure reflects growing concern across the technology industry about agentic AI systems, which are designed to work more independently and carry out complex tasks on behalf of users.Apple is not the first big tech company to flag the risk. Alphabet recently raised similar concerns in its own filing, and went further. It said it had seen unexpected behaviour during AI model testing, including agents acting outside their intended scope, which it warned could lead to “severe or catastrophic” security and societal incidents. Fortune noted that these warnings follow several major AI-related security incidents, most notably an attack on Hugging Face by OpenAI agents this summer. Anthropic’s IPO prospectus, made public last week, also lists cases where its models gained unauthorised access to real-world systems during security testing.Microsoft has announced controls to detect, monitor and restrict AI agents, including cutting their permissions or stopping them if they act suspiciously. CEO Satya Nadella has argued that companies should treat agents as potential insider risks and build security controls outside the AI model.Beyond AI safety concerns, Apple's filing also highlighted challenges related to its AI ambitions. The company said growing demand for cloud computing, storage and AI infrastructure is creating supply constraints, longer lead times and rising costs. Apple noted that shortages of memory and storage components are expected to intensify and could affect its AI rollout plans. The company added that research and development spending rose 32% year-over-year, driven in part by higher infrastructure costs and continued AI investments.Speaking after the company’s earnings announcement, CEO John Ternus explained that the agentic AI capabilities as promising tools for users but stressed that people must completely understand the access and permissions they grant such systems. Trenus also pointed out the Apple’s ocus on security and privacy as it continues developing AI-powered features and services.The warning underscores a broader shift across the technology sector as companies race to deploy increasingly capable AI agents while simultaneously acknowledging the security, privacy and operational risks that can emerge when autonomous systems gain greater access to data, software and real-world actions.
Article Summary: Apple warns that autonomous AI agents could access systems without authorisation, send communications, execute transactions and behave in unpredictable ways. The warning was included in the iPhone maker's latest annual 10-K filing, released a day after the company reported its fourth-quarter financial results. Apple also highlighted challenges related to its AI ambitions.

Article Title: Bus travel gets costlier in Karnataka: BMTC fares up 35%, KSRTC and other by 23%
Article Text:
Commuters will have to shell out more as Karnataka government announces a steep hike in bus fares across all four state-run transport corporations (SRTCs).





Bengaluru: A daily bus ride is set to burn a much bigger hole in the pockets of commuters, with the Karnataka government unleashing a steep and unprecedented fare hike across all four state-run transport corporations. From short city rides to long-distance journeys, passengers will have to shell out significantly more, with BMTC fares surging by 32% to 35% and those of KSRTC , NWKRTC and KKRTC going up by 23%. The steep revision is set to hit lakhs of daily commuters, particularly office-goers and low-income families who depend on public transport. The revised fares will come into effect from Thursday midnight (Nov 5).The scale of the hike is unprecedented! Between 2009 and 2025, fare revisions by the four corporations ranged from a modest 3.56% to a maximum of 15%, making the latest increase more than double the highest revision in the previous 16 years.In Bengaluru, even the shortest bus ride will cost significantly more. The minimum fare for city buses (BMTC), covering journeys of up to 2 km, has jumped from Rs 6 to Rs 10 — a 67% increase! Those travelling between 2 km and 4 km will have to pay Rs 6 more, while fares for longer distances have gone up by as much as Rs 12. A trip from Majestic to Shivajinagar, which earlier cost Rs 12, will now set passengers back by Rs 18. The Majestic-Yeshwanthpur and Majestic-Vijayanagar fares have climbed from Rs 18 to Rs 25, while commuters travelling to Attibele will have to shell out Rs 42 instead of Rs 30.The pinch will be equally severe for passengers using BMTC’s Vajra AC services. The first 6 km will cost Rs 5 more, journeys between 6 km and 18 km will attract a Rs 10 hike, while longer trips will become costlier by up to Rs 15.A journey from Central Silk Board to Hebbal will now cost Rs 65 against Rs 55, while the Majestic-Attibele fare has increased from Rs 60 to Rs 70.Passengers travelling beyond Bengaluru will also feel the heat. For KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC services, fares have been increased by Rs 9 for the first five stages and Rs 18 for journeys covering up to 10 stages. An ordinary bus journey from Bengaluru to Nelamangala or Hoskote will now cost Rs 44 against Rs 35 earlier. In express services, the Bengaluru-Nelamangala fare has risen from Rs 81 to Rs 100, while passengers travelling to Mandya will have to pay Rs 136 instead of Rs 110.Defending the steep increase, transport minister Byrathi Suresh cited escalating operational costs, including diesel prices, employee salaries and bus maintenance expenses. He said KSRTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC had revised fares only twice in the past 10 years, while BMTC had effected just one revision during the period.The minister said diesel prices alone had surged by Rs 10.47 per litre this year, adding to the mounting financial burden on the corporations. The four transport undertakings have accumulated liabilities of Rs 9,912 crore, including loans amounting to Rs 2,192 crore, he said.On the financial implications of the Shakti scheme, which provides free bus travel to women, Suresh maintained that it had not undermined the corporations’ financial health as the state government reimburses the expenditure. However, he admitted that the government was yet to clear Rs 6,200 crore in reimbursements due to the corporations under the scheme.
Article Summary: Karnataka government announces a steep hike in bus fares across all four state- run transport corporations. The steep revision is set to hit lakhs of daily commuters, particularly office-goers and low-income families who depend on public transport. The revised fares will come into effect from Thursday midnight (Nov 5)

Article Title: Weather tomorrow: IMD forecasts rain, thunderstorms in 8 states; Cyclone Murasu weakens into depression, winds up to 60 kmph likely
Article Text:
(Representative) The India Meteorological Department has predicted thunderstorms, gusty winds, and rainfall in several states

Cyclone Murasu weakens into depression, likely to weaken further

Delhi weather tomorrow

Tamil Nadu weather : Thunderstorms, heavy rain likely

Goa weather: Light rain, thundershowers likely

West Bengal weather: Temperatures to fall

Karnataka weather: Isolated showers expected

Rayalaseema weather: Rain, gusty winds likely

Madhya Pradesh weather: Rainfall forecast

Himachal Pradesh weather: Rain, snowfall likely in higher reaches

IMD's latest forecast for the next few days





NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and rainfall across several states over the next few days. Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to witness thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and isolated rainfall, while parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rayalaseema and Karnataka may also receive showers. Meanwhile, the remnant of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu has weakened into a depression over east Telangana and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh and is likely to weaken further into a well-marked low-pressure area over the next 12 hours.The deep depression, which is the remnant of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu, over coastal Andhra Pradesh and adjoining east Telangana moved nearly northwards at a speed of 10 kmph during the past six hours before weakening into a depression.According to the IMD, the system was centred over east Telangana and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh at 5.30 am IST on Wednesday (November 4), near latitude 17.0°N and longitude 80.1°E.It was located around 30 km northwest of Nandigama in Andhra Pradesh, 30 km south of Khammam in Telangana, 80 km northwest of Vijayawada, 90 km east of Nalgonda and 110 km southwest of Bhadrachalam.The depression is very likely to continue moving nearly northwards and weaken further into a well-marked low-pressure area during the next 12 hours.Delhi is likely to witness partly cloudy skies over the next few days, according to the IMD. No rainfall warning has been issued for the national capital. Punjab and Haryana are also expected to remain largely dry, offering residents some respite from changing weather conditions.Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph, reaching up to 60 kmph, along with isolated rainfall through November 8.Heavy rainfall is forecast at isolated places between November 6 and 7. For Wednesday (November 4), the IMD has forecast heavy rainfall in Madurai, Theni and Dindigul districts, while other parts of Tamil Nadu are expected to receive moderate rainfall.Rainfall activity is likely to remain concentrated in parts of western and southern Tamil Nadu, particularly districts adjoining the Western Ghats, where local weather conditions could contribute to heavier showers.Light rain and thundershowers are likely at isolated places over the ghats and adjoining areas of North Goa and Kushavati district on November 4 and 5.The IMD has forecast dry weather across West Bengal, with minimum temperatures likely to gradually fall by 3-4 degrees Celsius over the next three days.North Interior Karnataka is likely to receive isolated showers, according to the IMD forecast.Rayalaseema is expected to receive rainfall over the next few days, accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds. Wind speeds of 30-40 kmph, reaching up to 50 kmph, are likely.East and West Madhya Pradesh are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall, accompanied by gusty winds in some areas.Light to moderate rainfall has affected several parts of Himachal Pradesh under the influence of a Western Disturbance. Higher-altitude areas, including Kinnaur, Shimla and Lahaul-Spiti, may experience light snowfall.Isolated rain or snowfall is also possible in the higher reaches of Chamba and upper Kangra. The plains and mid-hill districts are likely to remain mainly clear from November 3, with temperatures expected to rise by 2-3 degrees Celsius over the next week.The IMD's latest forecast indicates continued rainfall and thunderstorm activity in parts of southern India, particularly Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, through November 8. Isolated showers are also expected in parts of Karnataka, Rayalaseema and Madhya Pradesh, while Goa may receive light rain and thundershowers on November 4 and 5.Meanwhile, West Bengal is likely to experience dry weather and falling minimum temperatures, while higher-altitude areas of Himachal Pradesh may see isolated snowfall. The depression over east Telangana and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh is also expected to weaken further into a well-marked low-pressure area within the next 12 hours.
Article Summary: The India Meteorological Department has predicted thunderstorms, gusty winds, and rainfall in several states. Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to witness thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds and isolated rainfall. Parts of Madhya Pradesh, Rayalaseema and Karnataka may also receive showers. The remnant of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu has weakened into a depression over east Telangana and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh.

Article Title: November pain: Air quality severe in parts of Delhi
Article Text:
North Delhi’s Jahangirpuri was the most polluted wi­th an AQI of 462

Weather adds to capital's air pollution woes

Poll Vote & Share your view How effective are current measures like GRAP-II in combating air pollution? Very Effective Somewhat Effective Not Effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: The city's air quality index read 350 at 4pm Tuesday - sliding further within the very poor category since Monday - while at least eight areas slipped into severe air quality. Monitoring agencies expect the rest of the city to deteriorate to severe air quality soon.North Delhi's Jahangirpuri was the most polluted with an AQI of 462, followed by Alipur (430), Bawana (421), DTU (445), Mundka (422), North Campus (405), Punjabi Bagh (449), and Vivek Vihar (425). Safdarjung, the base station, recorded very poor air quality.The share of stubble burning emissions from neighbouring states in Delhi's polluted air has increased, the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology has said.The decision support system's models showed 8.5% share of stubble burning Monday, expected to spike to 15.5% Tuesday. This would almost equal vehicular pollution, which dominates the city's emission inventory.IITM expects stubble burning contribution to rise to 20% by Nov 4 and 22% by Nov 5. The air quality is likely to be very poor or even severe in the next six days, IITM said.Air quality continued to deteriorate in several parts of the city despite GRAP-II restrictions in place from Monday. Experts said weather unfavourable for dispersal of pollutants was the major reason behind the spike.Temperatures were below normal in Delhi. The maximum at Safdarjung was 29.1 degrees Celsius, a notch below normal. The minimum was 16.4 degrees Celsius, a notch above normal. Met expects the maximum and minimum temperatures to hover between 27-29 and 14-16 degrees Celsius Wednesday.
Article Summary: The city's air quality index read 350 at 4pm Tuesday - sliding further within the very poor category since Monday. Monitoring agencies expect the rest of the city to deteriorate to severe air quality soon. North Delhi's Jahangirpuri was the most polluted with an AQI of 462, followed by Alipur (430), Bawana (421), DTU (445), Mundka (422), North Campus (405), Punjabi Bagh (449), and Vivek Vihar (425)

Article Title: Prepare plan to clean up waste along rail tracks: Centre to MCD
Article Text: New Delhi: Centre has directed MCD to prepare a comprehensive action plan within 15-20 days to clean up and manage legacy waste that has accumulated along 18.9km of railway stretches at 125 locations in Delhi.Delhi has a total railway track length of 365.2km.At a meeting chaired by the Union home secretary last week, the Railway Board chairperson flagged the accumulation of solid waste along railway tracks and adjoining areas, including unauthorised encroachments and colonies, which poses environmental hazards, health risks and operational safety threats. He called for a mechanism to prevent garbage from piling up on railway land.The meeting was convened to review Delhi’s cleanliness scenario under Special Campaign 6.0, following an earlier review of the campaign on Oct 19. DDA and NDMC officials were also present at the meeting.“The Union home secretary directed MCD to prepare a practical plan for daily door-to-door waste collection and its authorised disposal. The civic body was also asked to conduct a location-wise survey to assess daily waste generation and identify collection gaps,” stated the minutes of the meeting.Under the action plan, MCD, in coordination with the UT division and Railway Board, will map adjoining colonies and identify the sources contributing to waste dumping along railway tracks. “The exercise will also estimate the total waste generated from these areas and establish strict enforcement measures to prevent unauthorised dumping,” stated the minutes.Emphasis was laid on implementing door-to-door waste collection in all areas adjoining railway tracks, including unauthorised habitations, to ensure garbage does not accumulate on railway land. MCD and other agencies were also asked to launch an information, education and communication campaign to create public awareness and collaborate with local communities and NGOs.While MCD is carrying out the sanitation drives along the railways, it decided in March to engage a dedicated agency for regular waste removal for year-round cleanliness. It also planned to create garbage bins and collection points on railway land in consultation with residents, councillors and railway authorities.Indian Railways operates about 123km of railway tracks in the NCT of Delhi, with many stretches passing alongside slums and JJ colonies.
Article Summary: Delhi has a total railway track length of 365.2km. Indian Railways operates about 123km of railway tracks in the NCT of Delhi. Many stretches passing alongside slums and JJ colonies. MCD decided in March to engage a dedicated agency for regular waste removal.

Article Title: Anthropogenic emission cuts in Delhi-NCR could slash PM2.5 by 60%, study reveals
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A study by National Institute of Advanced Studies (NIAS) has proposed dividing India into 16 air-quality management regions, called “airshedem”, to implement targeted pollution control measures based on local geography and emissions. It found that controlling human-generated emissions in the heavily polluted region encompassing Delhi and neighboring states could reduce local PM2.5 concentrations by approximately 60% and lower the national average by 10%.Researchers identified India’s 16 distinct airshedems by analysing over two decades of climate data (2000–2023), satellite-derived pollution estimates, emission inventories and machine learning. To ensure practical pollution-control planning, the framework also integrates factors like land use, population density, economic activity, geology, public health, and administrative boundaries.“The characteristics of these regions reveal pronounced inequalities in pollution levels and sectoral emission contributions, where two of 16 airshedems, covering 23% of the landmass contribute 50% of the national PM2.5 and nitrogen oxide (Nox) source loads, with the residential, transportation and industrial sectors being the primary contributors,” said the study.The two highest-emitting regions were classified airshedem-2 (AS-2) and AS-7. AS-2 covers Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Chandigarh, and parts of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.The study, “Airshedem-Based Mitigation as a Pathway to Cleaner Air in India” by Ummed Singh Saharan and Gufran Beig, noted that AS-2’s elevated emissions stem from dense population, extensive agriculture, industrial and urban development, heavy transport, residential biofuels and crop burning. In contrast, AS-7’s pollution primarily comes from intensive coal and mineral mining, thermal power generation and automobile.According to the study, Airshedem-7 (AS-7) is one of the central and southern Indian airsheds. It is characterised by extensive forest cover and significant mining activity.The researchers simulated an emission-control scenario where anthropogenic emissions were shut off only in AS-2. This targeted intervention cut PM2.5 concentrations in AS-2 by 60%, reduced pollution in neighbouring regions by 5% to 17%, and dropped the national average by 10% (from 33 to 30 micrograms per cubic metre).Researchers found that even with all local human-caused emissions shut off in the model, AS-2’s background PM2.5 remained high at 21 micrograms per cubic metre. Pollution transported from neighbouring countries contributed roughly 5 micrograms per cubic metre to the region’s background concentration.“Controlling anthropogenic emissions within the critically important airshedem-2 alone could reduce PM2.5 concentrations by around 70% locally, 40% across the Indo-Gangetic Plain, and 10% at the national scale. Thus, this study presents the multidimensional framework beyond traditional climatology and environ-geographical parameters to include socio-economic and cultural factors, making a conceptual advancement over existing approaches,” said Beig.He added that strategically prioritising interventions according to the airshedem concept offers a pathway to improvements in air quality, enhanced public health outcomes, and progress toward environmental sustainability.
Article Summary: A study has proposed dividing India into 16 air-quality management regions, called ‘airshedem’ It found that controlling human-generated emissions in the heavily polluted region could reduce local PM2.5 concentrations by approximately 60% and lower the national average by 10%.

Article Title: Homeo colleges seek lower cut-offs amid vacant seats
Article Text: MUMBAI: With about 50% of undergraduate homeopathy seats and several postgraduate seats remaining vacant, the Principals Association of Homeopathic Medical Colleges of Maharashtra has urged the Union AYUSH ministry to lower the qualifying percentiles for the 2026 admission season. The association has argued that the existing cut-offs are preventing aspiring students from securing admission despite seats being available.In a representation to Union minister of state for AYUSH Prataprao Jadhav, the association has sought relaxation in qualifying criteria for Bachelor of Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS) and MD (Homeopathy) admissions for 2026-27. It has also requested that the relaxation be extended to subsequent and special stray vacancy rounds.The current NEET-UG qualifying cut-offs are 213 for the open category and 177 for reserved categories. For postgraduate admissions, the corresponding cut-offs are 136 and 119. Principals said seats are lying vacant even in government colleges and aided institutions. "An increase in MBBS and dental seats has affected our admission numbers too," said Dr Dharmendra Sharma, president of the association.The association has warned that vacant seats are affecting the financial sustainability of homeopathic colleges, which must meet substantial recurring expenditure on faculty salaries, hospital operations, laboratories and compliance with National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH) norms, irrespective of student intake.Several institutions, it said, are facing financial stress, delays in salary payments and difficulties retaining experienced faculty. Prolonged vacancies could threaten the functioning and, in some cases, survival of colleges.Dr Tarkeshwar Jain, NCH president, said, “The demand to reduce cut-offs is premature as several states are in the midst of their admission process and a decision cannot be taken right now.”Citing relaxations considered in other medical streams, including MBBS and BDS, to address vacant seats, the association has sought similar consideration for homeopathy without compromising basic eligibility or institutional standards.The principals' association has called for a long-term admission policy that takes into account student demand, vacant seats and institutional viability, arguing that the issue affects not just colleges but also students, employees and communities dependent on their healthcare services.
Article Summary: The Principals Association of Homeopathic Medical Colleges of Maharashtra has urged the Union AYUSH ministry to lower the qualifying percentiles for the 2026 admission season. The current NEET-UG qualifying cut-offs are 213 for the open category and 177 for reserved categories.

Article Title: ​FDA raids Dharashiv hub, seizes 1,830 kg khoya worth Rs5 lakh
Article Text:
Khoya stock seized by the FDA in Dharashiv district

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: Dharashiv, known as the khoya manufacturing hub of Marathwada, has come under the scanner of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as part of its ‘Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra’ campaign. Officials seized 1,830 kg of khoya worth Rs5 lakh from two units in Bhum taluka for various violations.“The action was taken against two dairy firms that supply khoya to sweet shops across Maharashtra, especially during the festive season. The licences of both manufacturers have been suspended,” FDA joint commissioner (food) Shrikaant Karkale said.At the first firm, FDA teams found 831 kg of khoya—718 kg packed in gunny bags and 113 kg loose—stored in unhygienic conditions. The stock, valued at Rs2,65,920, was sealed for violating Sections 23, 26, and 27 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.In the second raid, officials seized 999 kg of loose khoya packed in 50 plastic bags, valued at Rs2,39,760. The unit was found to be operating without a valid food licence or registration, in direct violation of food safety norms.Dharashiv district, particularly Bhum, Paranda, and Washi areas, has emerged as a major khoya production centre, with hundreds of quintals dispatched daily to different parts of the state.“Samples from both seized lots have been sent to the govt food testing laboratory. Strict legal action, including prosecution and heavy penalties, will follow if the lab report confirms adulteration or a failure to meet safety standards,” Karkale said.FDA seizes 2,916 kg of sweets worth Rs5 LakhIn another crackdown in Dharashiv district, the FDA seized 2,916 kg of suspected sweets worth Rs5,00,040 on Solapur–Dhule highway due to suspected adulteration and quality issues.Action was taken against a vehicle carrying the sweet items near Pandurang Hotel at Ratnapur in Kalamb taluka for the violation of Food Safety Act Sections 23, 26, and 27.The seizure included 838 kg of rabdi worth Rs1.67 lakh and 2,078 kg of “gulab jamun special mix” worth Rs3.32 lakh, FDA officials said.Stating that the ‘Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra’ campaign will continue with greater intensity, FDA officials emphasised that no compromise on food safety will be tolerated.
Article Summary: Dharashiv district, particularly Bhum, Paranda, and Washi areas, has emerged as a major khoya production centre. Officials seized 1,830 kg of khoya worth Rs5 lakh from two units in Bhum taluka for various violations.

Article Title: Six held for ‘digital arrest’ fraud that cost Latur senior citizen Rs 28.51 lakh
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Latur cyber police arrested six people from Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, and Haryana for allegedly operating mule bank accounts that cyber fraudsters used to cheat a 66-year-old retired BSNL official of Rs 28.51 lakh through a ‘digital arrest’ scam.The accused are Amit Shivnarayan Dubey (40) and Anurag Ganeshdatta Mishra (27), both residents of Katni, and Shivam Madhavsingh Thakur (24), a resident of Mandla district in Madhya Pradesh; Ankit Mansingh Yadav (32) and Kunalsingh Narendrasingh Rawat (30), both residents of Delhi; and Shivkumar Narendrasingh (30), a resident of Sector 45, Gurugram, Haryana.Police said the accused played a key role in transferring the money through multiple bank accounts on behalf of cyber criminals who impersonated police, Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials and threatened the retired official with arrest in a fabricated money laundering case.Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe said the arrests followed a technical investigation into the financial transactions and the bank accounts used to route the defrauded money. “The six accused allegedly operated mule bank accounts through which the money defrauded from the victim was routed. Their role in facilitating the financial transactions is being investigated. We are also tracing the money trail to identify the ultimate beneficiaries and establish the involvement of other members in the cyber fraud network,” he said.According to police, the retired man received calls from unidentified persons, who allegedly claimed that he was involved in a Rs 122-crore money-laundering case and had links with terrorists. The fraudsters threatened him with arrest, imprisonment and social disgrace, keeping him under sustained psychological pressure.Latur cyber police inspector Vivekanand Patil said, "The callers claimed that, as per Reserve Bank of India (RBI) directives, the money in his bank accounts had to be transferred for verification as part of the investigation. To make their claims appear genuine, they allegedly used a fabricated ED letter and convinced the retired BSNL official that transferring his funds was necessary to establish his innocence. Fearing legal consequences, the victim transferred around Rs 28.51 lakh into multiple bank accounts.”An FIR was registered at the Latur cyber police station on July 6 under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act. During the investigation, police analysed the financial transactions and traced the bank accounts allegedly used to receive and transfer the money, leading them to the six suspects.The accused were produced before the Judicial Magistrate First Class in Latur on Nov 1. Police sought their custody for further investigations in the case. The court remanded all six accused in police custody till Nov 6.
Article Summary: The accused are Amit Shivnarayan Dubey, Anurag Ganeshdatta Mishra, Shivam Madhavsingh Thakur, Ankit Mansingh Yadav and Kunalsingh Narendrasingh Rawat. Police said the accused played a key role in transferring the money through multiple bank accounts on behalf of cyber criminals.

Article Title: Pharmacists must lead fight against antibiotic misuse: Pratap Jadhav
Article Text:
Union minister of state for Ayush (independent charge) Pratap Jadhav at the event organised by PCI on Tuesday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Union minister of state for Ayush (independent charge) Pratap Jadhav on Tuesday called unnecessary use of antibiotics a major public health threat, urging pharmacists to take the lead in promoting the safe and rational use of medicines.Addressing a state-level function organised by Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) in association with MGM University’s department of pharmaceutical sciences and Y B Chavan College of Pharmacy, Jadhav said every pharmacy should serve as a trusted centre for medicine-related information and awareness. “Antimicrobial resistance is not limited to a single patient. It is a challenge for the entire society,” he said, warning that self-medication, altering treatment without medical advice and discontinuing medicines midway fuel drug-resistant infections, making even common illnesses difficult to treat.Highlighting the critical role of pharmacists in healthcare delivery, Jadhav said they must counsel patients on medicine quality, dosage, duration of treatment, method of use and possible side effects. He also urged pharmacists to encourage patients to complete prescribed courses and avoid sharing leftover medicines.The minister said emerging fields like digital health, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and drug research were creating new opportunities and stressed the need to update pharmacy education and training to keep pace with changing healthcare demands.PCI president Montukumar Patel said National Education Policy-aligned B Pharma curriculum now placed greater emphasis on clinical pharmacy, AI and advanced technologies. He said an industry-academia advisory board had been constituted to bridge the gap between education and industry requirements.Patel said provisions of around Rs 200 crore had been made for GPAT scholarships for MPharma students, while Rs 80 crore has been earmarked for research and skill development centres.
Article Summary: Pratap Jadhav urged pharmacists to take the lead in promoting the safe and rational use of medicines. “Antimicrobial resistance is not limited to a single patient. It is a challenge for the entire society,” he said. He said emerging fields like digital health, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and drug research were creating new opportunities.

Article Title: ​​Nanded division collect Rs 4.9 lakh during 16-hour ticket checking drive
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The Nanded division of the South Central Railway (SCR) collected Rs 4.9 lakh as fine and fare from 728 cases of ticketless and irregular travel during a massive ticket-checking drive conducted on Monday.The special drive was conducted from 4 am to 8 pm across the division involving Shailesh Kumar, assistant commercial manager, and 33 ticket-checking staff and two RPF personnel.“The squads checked 26 trains in total, including Devagiri Express, Nandigram Express, Rajya Rani Express, Shri Ganganagar Express, Sachkhand Express, Krishna Express, Bangalore Express, Vande Bharat Express and others,” Rajesh Shinde, chief publicity inspector of Nanded division of SCR, said.The ticket-checking drive generated Rs 4,87,120 in revenue. Officials detected 393 cases of ticketless travel, collecting Rs 1,78,825 in fares and Rs 1,97,130 in penalties.Another 96 cases of irregular travel yielded Rs 26,120 in fares and Rs 48,000 in penalties, while 239 cases of unbooked luggage attracted penalties amounting to Rs 37,045.The railway administration has appealed to the passengers to always carry valid tickets or authorised travel authority and travel only with proper class tickets. “Travelling without ticket or on wrong ticket is a punishable offence and penal action will be taken as per railway rules. Also, passengers have been advised not to buy tickets from unauthorized persons and not to travel on others’ tickets,” Shinde said.
Article Summary: The Nanded division of the South Central Railway collected Rs 4.9 lakh as fine and fare from 728 cases of ticketless and irregular travel. The special drive was conducted from 4 am to 8 pm across the division involving 33 ticket-checking staff and two RPF personnel.

Article Title: ​FDA seizes 2,280 litres of cow ghee worth Rs20 lakh over misbranding, adulteration suspicion
Article Text:
Ghee stock seized by FDA in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorities seized 2,279.7 litres of cow ghee of a popular brand from a godown in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on suspicion of being misbranded and adulterated.The raid was conducted on Sunday evening on the premises of the distributor located near Cambridge School at Sundarwadi.According to officials, the stock kept for sale was found suspicious and seized under Section 38(1)(c) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.“Prima facie, the stock was found to be misbranded and adulterated. Samples have been sent to the laboratory for analysis and further legal action will follow,” FDA joint commissioner (food) Shrikaant Karkale said. The licence of the oil repacking unit has been suspendedIn another action, FDA suspended the FSSAI licence of an oil repacking unit at Lasur in Gangapur taluka of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, and seized 2,710 kg refined soybean oil worth Rs 4.87 lakh. The unit scored only 30 out of 86 marks during inspection conducted by food safety officer Pragya Surse. Officials found it was operating as a repacker while its licence was for general manufacturing, with no lab reports, no food-grade packaging certificates, poor ventilation and lack of safety gear and mandatory records.
Article Summary: FDA seized 2,279.7 litres of cow ghee of a popular brand from a godown in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The stock was found to be misbranded and adulterated. FDA suspended the licence of an oil repacking unit in Gangapur taluka.

Article Title: Sharad Pawar hospitalised, calls off Marathwada tour
Article Text:
Partly cloudy skies over Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Monday

Pune/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

TOI





NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic on Monday following a bout of cough, cancelling his scheduled visit to drought-hit Marathwada.According to Dr Purvez Grant, chairman and managing trustee of the hospital, the veteran politician was admitted for a routine health evaluation and medical observation after complaining of pleuritic chest pain. “His condition is expected to settle down and he will remain under observation as a precautionary measure,” Grant said.Pawar’s daughter and Baramati MP Supriya Sule toldher father was stable and admitted to the hospital. “He is stable and all his parameters are normal” she said.The 85-year-old politician had toured Solapur on Sunday and was scheduled to reach Dharashiv on Monday evening before visiting Beed on Tuesday as part of an outreach programme in drought-affected areas. The tour was cancelled earlier in the day amid health concerns and a sudden change in weather conditions across the region.Meanwhile, India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast unseasonal rain across several parts of Marathwada over the next few days.Light to moderate showers are expected in Latur, Dharashiv and Nanded on Tuesday, with rainfall activity likely to intensify over the following 48 hours.Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna and Beed districts may also witness light rain and thundershowers, with wet weather expected to persist for at least two more days.Rainfall has already been reported from parts of the region, including Dharashiv (1.6mm) and Latur (0.6mm), while isolated areas in Beed also received showers during the 24 hours ending Monday morning.Weather experts at Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Agricultural University, Parbhani, attributed the unseasonal rainfall to Cyclonic Storm Murasu over the Bay of Bengal and associated weather systems. They said rainfall activity could continue in parts of Marathwada till Nov 4.The changing weather marks a sharp departure from the clear skies and rising temperatures seen across Marathwada last week.With all 76 talukas in the region officially declared drought-hit by state govt, the expected rainfall could provide some relief to parched agricultural areas, though its overall impact remains to be seen.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was admitted to Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic on Monday following a bout of cough. The 85-year-old politician had toured Solapur on Sunday and was scheduled to reach Dharashiv on Monday evening before visiting Beed on Tuesday. The tour was cancelled earlier in the day amid health concerns and a sudden change in weather conditions across the region.

Article Title: Cash instead of foodgrains: State approves DBT for APL farmers in 14 districts
Article Text:
A standard operating procedure (SOP) for the scheme has also been laid out by state govt

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The state govt has approved the onboarding of the direct benefit transfer (DBT) scheme for above poverty line (APL) saffron ration card-holding farmers in 14 farmer suicide-hit districts on the MahaDBT 2.0 portal.It has also laid down a standard operating procedure (SOP) for the scheme. Under the scheme, the benefit amount will be transferred to the Aadhaar-linked bank account of the woman head of the household. If there is no woman head, or if her account is not Aadhaar-linked, the amount will be credited to the account of a senior male member or another member of the family.The Aadhaar numbers of all members listed on the ration card must be linked to the Ration Card Management System (RCMS), and e-KYC of every beneficiary is mandatory. Tehsil offices will guide members who do not have Aadhaar cards on the process of obtaining them.The govt resolution (GR), issued by the food, civil supplies and consumer protection department on Oct 30, covers Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Nanded, Beed, Dharashiv, Parbhani, Latur, Hingoli, Amravati, Washim, Akola, Buldhana, Yavatmal, and Wardha. According to the GR, eligible farmers not covered under the National Food Security Act, 2013, will receive Rs 170 per beneficiary per month in cash instead of foodgrains.The scheme was re-engineered under govt process re-engineering and onboarded on MahaDBT 2.0 (mahadbt2.maharashtra.gov.in) to make it more transparent, faster, error-free and integrated.A department secretary-led review meeting on Jan 22-23, 2025, decided to route the scheme through MahaIT-run direct benefit transfer. Approved through a Feb 28, 2023, GR, it provided Rs 150 monthly from Jan 2023. A June 20, 2024, circular raised this to Rs 170 from April 2024. The GR also referred to an earlier GR dated July 24, 2015.The GR states that “the amount will be revised every year in line with hikes in the minimum support price, as per the Cash Transfer of Food Subsidy Rules, 2015, notified by the Centre. The revised sum will be rounded off to the next multiple of Rs 10”.Under the SOP, data of eligible ration card holders on the Ration Card Management System (RCMS) will be given to Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Ltd. It will then flow automatically to MahaDBT 2.0 through the Mahasarathi system. Officials at taluka, district and state levels will get logins.Taluka-level officers will check RCMS data month-wise, financial year-wise and fair price shop-wise. They will select an eligible member with an Aadhaar-linked bank account, preferably the woman head of the family, and forward the application to the district. If she has no such account, another member's Aadhaar-linked account will be chosen. District-level officers (DSO) will scrutinise the applications and either give bulk approval or reject them with reasons if defects are found.The state nodal officer (SNO) will complete the “allocate beneficiaries” process after checking the number of approved beneficiaries by financial year and instalment, and the admissible funds. The SNO will then generate a bill or Request for Transfer (RFT) and submit it to the drawing and disbursing officer (DDO). The DDO will digitally sign the RFT, generate and digitally sign an XML file and trigger payment. Rs 170 per member per month will then be credited to Aadhaar-linked accounts.The benefit is to be disbursed through MahaDBT 2.0 from April 2026. New ration card holders will become eligible from the month after their RCMS registration is completed.
Article Summary: The state govt has approved the onboarding of the direct benefit transfer (DBT) scheme for above poverty line (APL) saffron ration card-holding farmers in 14 farmer suicide-hit districts. It has also laid down a standard operating procedure (SOP) for the scheme. The benefit is to be disbursed through MahaDBT 2.0 from April 2026.
